utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The hearing's open. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Case Number IT-97-25/1-PT, the Prosecutor versus Mitar Rasevic and Savo Todovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Appearances for the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. For the Prosecution, my colleague, Ms. Christina Moeller, and my name is Hildegard Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Appearances for Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Hello, Your Honour. I am Vladimir Domazet, counsel for Mitar Rasevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Aleksandar Lazarevic, and I represent Mr. Savo Todovic before this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I greet everybody in this courtroom. Last time we met was 22 June this year, so it is about four months. Therefore I extend greetings to all members of the Prosecution and the Defence, Mr. Domazet, Mr. Lazarevic, and Mr. -- the accused. I apologise in the name of the former Chamber, which obliged us to start this hearing with practically half an hour delay inasmuch as the Oric Chamber had to finish with a witness because this witness has to take a plane tomorrow morning. And if they had postponed that until tomorrow morning, the witness in question could not have taken his plane. So they had to extend the hearing by a half an hour, which explains why you have had to wait and I have had to wait also. So this hearing is now starting today, and I wish to recall that according to the Rules, the Pre-Trial Judge shall convene a Status Conference within 120 days of the initial appearance of the accused. And since the last time was the 22nd of June, we have to meet again. So I will examine the motions which may be pending and also see about the documents -- a question of disclosure. As you know, after a motion from the Prosecution the Referral Bench by a decision of 8 July 2005 referred the case to the authorities of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the judicial authorities, by application applying Article 11 bis of the Rules. But the Defence of the accused Todovic, as well as the Prosecution, appealed from this decision on the 8th of July, 2005. And therefore, we are waiting on all sides the decision of the Chamber of appeal after the appeals which have been filed. For the other motions which are pending there is still one which is on stand-by. It's a preliminary motion of the Defence of Todovic, accused, which was filed on the 10th of March, 2005, applying Article 72(A)(ii) of the Rules. I will recall in my memory that on the 23rd of March, 2005, the Chamber had accepted the motion -- had granted the -- it was to have a stay of a decision on the motion of the accused Todovic on the 10th of March, 2005, awaiting a motion from the Prosecution to be allowed to modify -- to amend the indictment. And then on the 17th of May, 2005, the Chamber took an order asking the Prosecutor to establish a new indictment. On 25th of May, 2005, the Prosecution filed a motion asking the Chamber leave to amend the indictments. The Defence of the accused Todovic as well as the Defence for Todovic [as interpreted] filed their submissions following Article 72 of the Rules. On the 4th of July and 10th July, 2005, the Prosecution and the Defence of the accused filed respectively their response -- their replies. The Judges of the Chamber, whom I consulted, considered that one should await the decision on the question of the referral of the case to the judicial authorities of Bosnia-Herzegovina, because if this case were finally referred to the authorities of Bosnia-Herzegovina, it will be for the Prosecutor -- the local Prosecutor to draft an indictment since the referral has been ordered from a case file concerning facts. And the legal qualification of facts will be then done by the local prosecutor. Therefore, it appears to me difficult for the Judges of the Chamber to pronounce on legal issues when the local prosecutor has still to decide on these things according to his own indictment. This is the reason why we decided to await the decision of the Referral Bench. Since the Referral Bench has now to await a appeal we have to wait serenely the decision of the Appeals Chamber. As from that there will be two possibilities. One, if the Chamber of appeal confirms -- affirms the decision of the 8th of July, 2005, this will mean that this case is indeed referred to the Bosnia-Herzegovinian authorities. And therefore, the Chamber to which I belong will make a decision, citing that he will not have to rule on the matters of law since it will be the local bench we shall have -- the local prosecutor who will have to draft the indictment. On the other hand, if the Appeals Chamber decided that the case will stay with ICTY, henceforth in the next following days -- in the ten next following days we will render our own decision on the motion which is presently pending. And therefore, there will be no prejudice for any of the accused inasmuch as we will be in a position to render our decision. So I wanted to inform the parties of this question, this issue, because I consider that it's not necessary if the case is referred to another court, I don't think we should have to decide about the legal definitions when -- in a case in which the local prosecutor may have to draft his own indictment pursuant to Bosnia-Herzegovina law. Therefore, this being said, I will now speak about the disclosure. You got Article 66(A)(i) and (A)(ii) and Article 68 of the Rules, Rule 68. And I will give the floor to here from each side what are the requests or comments. First of all, I am going to ask the Prosecution whether the disclosures according to Rule 66(A)(i) have been done and are continuing or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, according to my knowledge, nothing is outstanding in relation to the disclosure obligation that we have. What we do at the moment, though, is we review according to a decision of the trial -- of the Chamber the Krnojelac confidential materials and redact them and we'll soon provide them to counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you very much. Let me -- the Prosecution have to say that regarding Rule 66(A)(i) there was no problem, but the Prosecution team is planning to disclose confidential material from the Krnojelac case as soon as possible. Now, Mr. Domazet, do you have any comments?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] None at all, Your Honour. None whatsoever. No problem whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Perhaps this Honourable Trial Chamber is familiar with the fact that the Defence of Mr. Todovic filed actually three motions for access to confidential files in three different cases. One of the cases is Krnojelac case and I have just discussed with the Prosecution about the progress in this -- in this case. And I have assurance from the Prosecution that it is going to be given to me very soon and I don't have a problem with this. The other case was Milosevic case, the decision by the Trial Chamber is -- Milosevic case is rendered on this access and I'm waiting for this document to be handed over to me. The third case is Krajisnik case, and I can confirm that I have already received confidential documents from Krajisnik case, so I see no problem regarding disclosure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Thank you very much, Mr. Lazarevic, for this explanation regarding the three motions. One of them is going to be settled very soon. As regards the Milosevic case and the Krajisnik case, you hope to receive material very soon. Now we have to tackle the issue of Rule 66(A)(ii), that is disclosure by the Prosecutor to the Defence of various statements. In this respect as well, did you have any problems? Unless this is also settled by the motions for the Krnojelac, Milosevic, and Krajisnik cases. Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, to my knowledge nothing is outstanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No problems. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [In English] No problem. [Interpretation] Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Same thing, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very good. Rule 68. As you know, this is the rule that imposes on the Prosecution to disclose to the Defence any material which in the actual knowledge of the Prosecutor may suggest the innocence or mitigate the guilt of the accused or affect the credibility. So either you have documents as of now, or you have material coming from other cases that might possibly have an impact on the two accused here. So I'll first turn to the Prosecution to ask where we are.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, most of the exculpatory material or potential exculpatory material actually relates to the Krnojelac case, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. which is basically the same case as these accused have in front of themselves. And we have turned over a huge chunk of material from this case. The thing outstanding is what I already mentioned, disclosure of confidential materials, that needs to be done and will be finished soon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Now turning to the Defence regarding exculpatory material that might suggest the innocence in part or total of your clients. I know you always have problems, and this can raise problems. First, Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. No problem in this respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: To be frank, I see no problem. The only issue is that when we receive the disclosure from the Prosecution it is not clearly marked whether some of these documents are exculpatory and fell under Rule 68 or some other reason for disclosure exists. So -- but basically, we don't have this as a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Before moving on to the questions I always ask of the accused regarding their health and the detention conditions, I want to ask the parties whether they have any comments or problems they want to mention during this Status Conference. Let's start with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, nothing arises.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Domazet, do you have any problems?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, none whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: My client asked me earlier this morning to raise this issue before the Trial Chamber. It is not a big problem, but we couldn't resolve it so far. Some four and a half months ago I brought one laptop computer to the Detention Unit in order to enable my client to cooperate with myself, to prepare his defence in the most efficient way. So far he still hasn't received this laptop. I was trying on two or three occasions to -- and actually, I did contact with some officials of the UNDU. The last information that I received was a month ago, and I was informed that there is a new policy regarding some laptop computers and the possibility of the detainees to receive laptop computers. Also, I received information that the person who is in charge for checking these laptop computers was ill and that he wasn't able to work. So my client asked me to ask for assistance of the Trial Chamber in order to resolve this because it's been four and a half months since I brought it to the Detention Unit and he still hasn't received it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Lazarevic, thank you very much for raising this issue. Some time ago in a previous case, in the Dragomir Milosevic case, the same issue was raised, namely, that an accused received from relatives or from somebody outside the Tribunal a computer, a laptop, and a question was why he could not use the computer straight away. In the case of Dragomir Milosevic, on that very day, as I'm by the way about to do in the next few minutes, I sent a memo to the registrar asking for some explanation. So rest assured, straight away, without further ado, I will look into this. From what I could understand, generally speaking, it seemed that the Registry, because there's a new policy in terms of communications using an electronic means to send documents, I was saying that the Registry is planning to give to all accused presently in detention a computer each. It will be provided by the Tribunal. As to computers coming from another source than the Tribunal, which seems to be your case, the Registry has to make some checks on the computer in question. It should not be rigged or, you know, that sort of thing. You can understand that. That is basically for security reasons. There may be a major problem if the person in charge of checking it falls ill. Apparently this person has been ill for four months or has been on holiday, I don't know. Whatever the reason may be, this small check could have been done a long time ago. I'm not going to do it myself - after all I could do it - however this is not provided by the Rules. Our Deputy Registrar -- or court deputy could do it himself, but I'm sure we're going to find a solution very soon. I promise you that in the next few minutes I'll put the question to the Registrar and I shall send you, Mr. Lazarevic, a copy of my memo. This being said -- regarding computers, do you have any other comments or observations, starting with the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. And I'm grateful for your assistance in this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Now, Mr. Rasevic, would you mind standing up. As you know, we've been meeting regularly for a while and I always put the same questions to you, but I have to, hoping that everything is running smoothly. Regarding your state of health, do you have any particular problems? THE ACCUSED RASEVIC: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I don't have any health or family problems. My family visit me regularly. Only if you could allow me, I would kindly ask you the following. All this has been going very slowly, even the 11 bis procedure has been taking time. So I would kindly ask you in your capacity as a Judge to see what is happening. I would like things to be accelerated, if possible, and I would like my case to go to trial, either here or in Sarajevo. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Rasevic. Now, as to the Rule 11 bis matter, you know what I think of it. I've said that to you several times. You know there is a procedure that has been worked out by the Judges of this Tribunal. They decided to set up a special Referral Bench in order to rule on such matters. And as you said yourself, this has caused some delays. I personally thought that the Rule 11 bis procedure could have been settled by the Trial Chamber hearing the case. And in which case, you would have had a decision long ago. But the other Judges decided otherwise. So now we have to wait for a decision by the Appeals Chamber. I hope it will come soon. Do you have another question? THE ACCUSED RASEVIC: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. In any case, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Please sit down. Now, Mr. Todovic, please stand up. I have the same question of you, the same two questions. Your state of health and the detention conditions, what do you have to say? THE ACCUSED TODOVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my health condition is satisfactory. The conditions in the Detention Unit are at the highest level. I don't have any objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you have another matter you want to raise? Feel free to ask any question you wish. THE ACCUSED TODOVIC: [Interpretation] No, thank you, Your Honour. The only thing is the issue that has been raised by my lawyer, and that is the issue of the computer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Please sit down. THE ACCUSED TODOVIC: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So this brings us to the end of this Status Conference. As you noticed, the Prosecution and Defence, we're all awaiting the Appeals Chamber decision. Should the Appeals Chamber issue a ruling soon, and there's no reason why it shouldn't do so, then you have two possibilities if the case is referred. The pre-trial stage will be completed, will come to an end, by me. I will note that a decision has been made, in which case we won't see each other again. However, were the Appeals Chamber to decide that the case should stay with the ICTY, without any delay I shall convene on the parties, the Prosecution and you, and I promise to issue a decision within the next days as to this pending motion. And I will give, straight away, a deadline to the Prosecution for the filing of the pre-trial brief, the witness list, and the exhibit list so that this whole case can be trial-ready and for a Trial Chamber to try the case, because the accused have been waiting for a long time for a trial. So this is all I can tell you today. The hearing will be adjourned very soon so that I can turn to this memo I want to send to the Registrar. Thank you very much. The hearing stands adjourned.
